## Natural history notes

A tiny yellowish outdoor cockroach characterized by its small size, pale tan to yellow-brown body, long antennae, and delicate flattened shape. In Florida, Cariblatta lutea occurs in a variety of natural habitats, including pine scrub, flatwoods, hammocks, open pinelands, and marshy or leaf-litter areas, where it shelters under bark, in duff, and among low vegetation. It feeds as a scavenger on decaying plant material, fungi, algae, and other organic debris, helping recycle nutrients while serving as prey for spiders, lizards, birds, and predatory insects.
